questions.question: Which sequential condition is equivalent to continuity in the sequential characterization of continuity?
options: If $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)\to\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$, then $\boldsymbol{x}_i$ is constant
Every sequence in $\boldsymbol{X}$ must converge
If $\boldsymbol{x}_i\to\boldsymbol{x}_0$, then $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)\to\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$
Every image sequence must be eventually constant

questions.question: In the open-set formulation of continuity, what operation appears?
options: Taking images of open sets
Taking complements only in $\mathbb{R}$
Taking derivatives of open sets
Taking preimages of open sets

questions.question: Suppose $\boldsymbol{f}$ is continuous and $\boldsymbol{x}_i\to\boldsymbol{x}_0$. What should happen to $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)$?
options: It must diverge
It must be equal to $\boldsymbol{x}_i$
It converges to $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$
It must be open

questions.question: To show that $\boldsymbol{f}$ is not continuous at $\boldsymbol{x}_0$, what kind of sequence is useful?
options: A sequence $\boldsymbol{x}_i$ that never enters $\boldsymbol{X}$
A sequence of open sets whose images under $f$ are open
A sequence $\boldsymbol{x}_i\to\boldsymbol{x}_0$ for which $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)$ does not converge to $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$
A constant image sequence

questions.question: Which image/preimage distinction is important for continuity?
options: A continuous function may map an open set to a non-open set
A continuous function always maps open sets to open sets
A continuous function never has open preimages
A continuous function maps every subset to a closed set

questions.question: Which closed-set condition is equivalent to continuity in the sequential characterization of continuity?
options: The preimage of any closed set in $\boldsymbol{Y}$ is closed in $\boldsymbol{X}$
The image of any closed set in $\boldsymbol{X}$ is closed in $\boldsymbol{Y}$
Every closed set in $\boldsymbol{Y}$ is empty
Every subset of $\boldsymbol{X}$ is closed

questions.question: For the constant function $f(x) = 1$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and $V = (0,1)$, what is $f(V)$?
options: $\mathbb{R}$
$\varnothing$

questions.question: For $F = [1,+\infty)$ and $f(x) = \frac{1}{x}$ for $x \gt 0$, what is the image $f(F)$?
In the sequential formulation, why is the phrase 'for any convergent sequence' important?
options: Only constant sequences are allowed
The theorem applies only to divergent sequences
Sequences are irrelevant in metric spaces
One well-behaved sequence is not enough to prove continuity

questions.question: Which setting is assumed in the sequential characterization of continuity?
options: Only the domain is a finite set
Only functions from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ are allowed
Both domain and codomain are metric spaces
The codomain has no metric

questions.question: You want to prove $\boldsymbol{f}\colon\boldsymbol{X}\to\boldsymbol{Y}$ is continuous using open sets. Which task matches the sequential characterization of continuity?
options: Show that $\boldsymbol{f}(U)$ is open for every open $U\subseteq\boldsymbol{X}$
Show that every open set in $\boldsymbol{X}$ is empty
Show that $\boldsymbol{f}^{-1}(U)$ is closed for every open $U\subseteq\boldsymbol{Y}$
Show that $\boldsymbol{f}^{-1}(U)$ is open in $\boldsymbol{X}$ for every open $U\subseteq\boldsymbol{Y}$

questions.question: A sequence $\boldsymbol{x}_i\to\boldsymbol{x}_0$ is found, but $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)$ does not converge to $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$. What does the sequential characterization of continuity allow you to conclude?
options: $\boldsymbol{f}$ is continuous everywhere
$\boldsymbol{x}_i$ did not converge to $\boldsymbol{x}_0$
The preimage of every closed set is closed
$\boldsymbol{f}$ is not continuous at $\boldsymbol{x}_0$

questions.question: Which set-based condition is equivalent to continuity using open sets?
options: The preimage of every open set in the codomain is open in the domain.
The image of every open set in the domain is open in the codomain.
The preimage of every open set is empty.
The image of every closed set is closed in every case.

questions.question: Which set-based condition is equivalent to continuity using closed sets?
options: The preimage of every closed set in the codomain is closed in the domain.
The image of every closed set in the domain is open in the codomain
The preimage of every closed set is the whole domain
The image of every closed set must be finite.

questions.question: In the sequential formulation of continuity at $\boldsymbol{x}_0$, what must $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)$ converge to?
options: $\boldsymbol{x}_0$
$\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$
An arbitrary point independent of $\boldsymbol{x}_0$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{f}$ be continuous and let $U$ be open in the codomain. What can be concluded about $\boldsymbol{f}^{-1}(U)$?
options: It is closed in the codomain.
It is always empty.
It is always the entire codomain.
It is open in the domain.

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{f}$ be continuous and let $C$ be closed in the codomain. What can be concluded about $\boldsymbol{f}^{-1}(C)$?
options: It is open in the codomain.
It must be a singleton.
It must be empty.
It is closed in the domain.

questions.question: If $\boldsymbol{x}_i=\boldsymbol{x}_0$ for every $i$, what is the image sequence under any function $\boldsymbol{f}$?
options: It is constantly $\boldsymbol{x}_0$.
It is constantly $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$.
It must diverge.
It is undefined for every $i$.

questions.question: How can the sequential formulation be used to disprove continuity at $\boldsymbol{x}_0$?
options: Find one point whose image is open.
Find a closed set whose image under $f$ is also a closed set
Find any sequence in the codomain.
Find a sequence $\boldsymbol{x}_i\to\boldsymbol{x}_0$ for which $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)$ does not converge to $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$.

questions.question: Suppose $\boldsymbol{x}_i\to\boldsymbol{x}_0$ but $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_i)\to\boldsymbol{y}\ne\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{x}_0)$. What follows?
options: $\boldsymbol{f}$ is continuous at $\boldsymbol{x}_0$.
$\boldsymbol{x}_i$ does not converge to $\boldsymbol{x}_0$.
$\boldsymbol{f}^{-1}$ must exist as a function.
$\boldsymbol{f}$ is not continuous at $\boldsymbol{x}_0$.
